name: Frank Luntz

summary.text: Frank Luntz is an American pollster and political messaging consultant. A memo prepared by his firm for Republican politicians during George W. Bush's first term, titled "The Environment: A Cleaner, Safer, Healthier America" and obtained by the Environmental Working Group, advised that the lack of scientific certainty be kept a primary issue in the climate debate and that "climate change" be used in place of "global warming." On July 25, 2019, Luntz testified before the Senate Democrats' Special Committee on the Climate Crisis that he had been wrong and asked lawmakers to stop relying on his earlier work.

facts.claim: The Luntz memo advised Republican leaders to "continue to make the lack of scientific certainty a primary issue in the debate," and stated: "Should the public come to believe that the scientific issues are settled, their views about global warming will change accordingly."
facts.quote: continue to make the lack of scientific certainty a primary issue in the debate ... Should the public come to believe that the scientific issues are settled, their views about global warming will change accordingly.

facts.claim: The memo stated that "the scientific debate is closing [against us] but not yet closed. There is still a window of opportunity to challenge the science," and that "Voters believe that there is no consensus about global warming within the scientific community."

facts.claim: The memo warned Republican leaders they were losing "the environmental communications battle" and advised dropping "global warming" in favor of "climate change."
facts.quote: the memo warned Republican party leaders that they were losing "the environmental communications battle." It advised them to emphasize a lack of scientific certainty and drop "global warming" for the less scary-sounding "climate change."

facts.claim: On July 25, 2019, Luntz testified before the Senate Democrats' Special Committee on the Climate Crisis at a hearing titled "The Right Thing To Do: Conservatives for Climate Action," saying he was wrong in 2001 and asking lawmakers to stop relying on his earlier work because it was not accurate today.
facts.quote: he told the Senate committee he was wrong in 2001. He also asked lawmakers to stop relying on his earlier work, saying it was not accurate today.

facts.claim: In the 2019 testimony Luntz urged Democrats to "personalize, individualize and humanize" climate impacts and to drop language describing the problem as a crisis, and distanced himself from a June 2019 poll on Republican support for a carbon tax, saying it was not his and that he had left the firm bearing his name 18 months earlier.
facts.quote: Luntz urged Democrats to "personalize, individualize and humanize" the impacts of climate change. He also told them to "jettison" language like describing the problem as a crisis.

openQuestions: The memo's date is given as 2001, 2002 or 2003 in different sources; the Carbon Ledger page uses 2002. The memo text is hosted on a personal blog (sindark.com), not an official repository; EWG's original posting was not located.
No source returned links Luntz to the Koch network, ExxonMobil or the American Petroleum Institute, so no such connection is recorded.
Luntz's 2019 testimony PDF is on Sen. Schatz's site; the quoted passages come from press coverage of the hearing.
